rubrics.criterion: In the network interface's generic IP egress dispatch path, link-layer destination resolution is re-established as a separate responsibility that the dispatch path calls: the broadcast/multicast hardware-address derivation, the neighbor-cache lookup, and the unknown-neighbor resolution request (ARP request or IPv6 neighbor solicitation that consumes the transmit token and defers the packet) are no longer multi-level inline logic duplicated per medium branch, and both the IEEE 802.15.4 side and the Ethernet side of that dispatch path reach one shared resolution implementation.
rubrics.rationale: This is one of the four areas the task prompt asks to restore; the injected state re-created the resolution stage per medium branch, so the repair must make one shared seam serve both.

rubrics.criterion: The 6LoWPAN ingress path over IEEE 802.15.4 separates its absorbed stages: fragment reception with reassembly-slot management (acceptance guards, reassembly key/size bookkeeping, reassembly timeout, assembler feeding) and the IPHC/NHC decompression stage (IPv6 header re-materialization, extension-header and UDP expansion, length correction) become separately callable functions, and the decompression stage is one implementation shared by the direct-reception path and the fragment-reassembly path rather than two parallel copies.
rubrics.rationale: The ingress area absorbed a four-level helper chain; restoring it means the reassembled-first-fragment flow and the direct IPHC flow run the decompression stage once, not one per arrival path.

rubrics.criterion: The 6LoWPAN egress path over IEEE 802.15.4 separates its absorbed stages: the compressed-size accounting that feeds the fragmentation decision, the IPv6-to-IPHC compression and emission stage, and the FRAG1/FRAGN fragmentation plan (datagram-tag allocation, first-fragment sizing, datagram-size and offset rules) become separately callable functions, with the sizing and compression work shared by the fragmented and the non-fragmented send paths rather than re-derived per transmit path.
rubrics.rationale: The egress area absorbed sizing, compression and fragmentation planning into one funnel and re-created work across the two send paths; the repair restores stage units and removes the per-path duplication.

rubrics.criterion: The DHCPv4 client socket's inbound processing re-establishes ACK interpretation as one shared implementation — lease-parameter validation, configuration assembly, and the RFC 2131 renew/rebind/expiry timeline derivation — reached by both the Requesting-state arm and the Renewing-state arm, instead of a re-created copy of the interpretation logic inside each state arm.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state duplicated the absorbed ACK parser once per client-state arm; the prompt asks to collapse per-branch copies into one shared implementation.

rubrics.criterion: The four areas are not 'repaired' by relocating their monolithic bodies: the patch must not merely hoist a collapsed multi-stage body (wholesale or near-wholesale) into a new function and leave the top-level method a thin full-parameter delegator, and none of the extracted functions should itself interleave several distinct protocol stages the way the former monoliths did; moving code without separating stages counts as failure for this item.
rubrics.rationale: This is the case's central trap: a cut-and-delegate whole-body extraction compiles and preserves behavior but leaves the collapsed structure intact, so extraction that merely relocates the monolith must be recognized as unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: Each collapsed stage copy is actually removed once the shared implementation is restored: in the three touched production files, no medium branch, client-state arm, or send/receive path still executes its own inlined copy of a stage that now exists as a shared function, and no dead duplicate of a collapsed stage (including commented-out or test-only-caller remnants of it) remains behind.
rubrics.rationale: Half-dedup — a new shared stage created while one branch keeps its private copy — still passes the unit suite because every copy behaved identically, so only patch review catches the leftover.

rubrics.criterion: Feature gating is preserved for the combinations the default build exercises only as disabled code: the cfg attributes that sat on the absorbed stage fragments (medium and protocol-family gates around resolution and dispatch arms, hop-by-hop and routing-header sizing, medium-gated emissions) are present and correctly placed in the repaired structure, so enabling those features still selects the same protocol behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The default-feature test suite cannot observe non-default combinations; a repair that drops or misplaces a cfg gate would break them silently, and the prompt requires feature gates to stay as they are.

rubrics.criterion: The patch adds no new public API surface: every newly introduced stage helper keeps the weakest visibility its callers require (crate-, module- or parent-module-private like the surrounding sibling code), and no pre-existing public signature, type or trait is changed; call sites are re-wired through internal reachability, not through promoted visibility.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt's compatibility boundary demands no public API change; visibility promotion is the easy way to make new helpers reachable and must be recognized as a boundary violation.

rubrics.criterion: The re-established stages are placed and named the way the surrounding code organizes such work: codec logic sits with sibling codec logic in the same module rather than inside foreign paths, free functions stay free functions where the module keeps codec-free helpers at file scope, and the new names use the file's existing domain vocabulary (sizing, compression, decompression, interpretation).
rubrics.rationale: Beyond correctness, the repair's seams should read as native repository structure; this measures whether the solver respected the project's conventions rather than imposing an external layout.

rubrics.criterion: Comments in the touched paths match the produced structure: none of the injected flow-management prose that narrates whole stages living together (or the auxiliary notes that tie stage pieces together, such as explaining that a sizing result feeds a decision right below, or that every rejection path exits in one half of a block) survives in a place where the claimed arrangement no longer holds, and the RFC-citing notes for fragment sizing and lease timing stay attached to the code that implements them.
rubrics.rationale: The state left behind merged-flow narration that matches the monoliths, not repaired code; the prompt explicitly requires notes to end up consistent with the structure the solver produces.

rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves no orphaned scaffolding of its own: every function the patch introduces has a live caller on some path, and the import/use lists of the touched modules contain no item that only served relocated or collapsed-away code.
rubrics.rationale: Extractions gone wrong leave unused helpers and stale imports behind while the suite still passes; this verifies the cleanup actually converged.

rubrics.criterion: The patch introduces no padding or off-scope churn: no new file or module of trivial pass-through wrappers, no wholesale reformatting or no-op reordering of code outside the four areas, and no helper layer whose only effect is renaming an otherwise unchanged body.
rubrics.rationale: Distinguishes a focused structural repair from patches that disguise small work behind unrelated churn or insert indirection that adds no separation.

rubrics.criterion: Unknown-neighbor handling is not narrowed or dropped: for an un-resolved destination address the repaired dispatch path still transmits exactly one resolution request (ARP request for IPv4 over Ethernet, neighbor solicitation for the IEEE 802.15.4 / IPv6 cases), still consumes the transmit token while deferring the original packet, still returns the interface's not-ready consequence so the packet is retried, and keeps the neighbor cache's rate limiting active.
rubrics.rationale: The resolution stage is the riskiest piece of the extraction; a silently-dropped or doubled resolution request still passes much of the suite but changes protocol behavior the prompt freezes.

rubrics.criterion: Reassembly and decompression contracts are intact: datagrams whose decompressed size would fall below the IPv6 header size are still dropped; fragment reassembly keys still identify a datagram by link-layer source, tag and size; the reassembly deadline is still measured from packet arrival with the configured timeout; the first fragment still drives decompression through the reassembly stage so a fully reassembled datagram yields the complete decompressed packet; and malformed compressed input still results in a silent drop or assembler error with no new panic path.
rubrics.rationale: These reassembly invariants sit inside the deepest absorbed chain and are the easiest to disturb while restructuring buffer ownership; the prompt freezes exact protocol behavior including edge cases.

rubrics.criterion: Lease handling is intact: the RFC 2131 timeline derivation keeps its defaults (renew at half the lease, rebind at seven eighths) and the gap-based fallbacks when only one timer is offered, keeps the configured maximum-lease cap applied to the received duration, keeps the DNS list cleanup that drops non-unicast entries, keeps a Requesting ACK moving the socket to the Renewing state and a Renewing ACK preserving the existing rebinding flag with refreshed timer instants, and keeps the configuration-change signal raised in the same relation to the state update as before.
rubrics.rationale: The ACK-interpretation stage carries the riskiest duplicated arithmetic in the socket; merging the two arms wrongly (for example resetting state that must carry over) is the concrete near-miss for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The verification surface is untouched: no unit test, documentation test, assertion, test helper, feature declaration, example or bench is modified, removed, skipped, weakened or newly gated off anywhere in the patch.
rubrics.rationale: Making protocol-behavior edits pass by adjusting the suite is the most tempting shortcut when a repair changes behavior unintentionally; the prompt explicitly keeps every test out of scope.

rubrics.criterion: Behavior the repair merely passes through is not silently altered: the generic dispatch path's IPv4-fragmentation bookkeeping (length accounting per emitted fragment, offset advancement, the deciding conditions for fragmenting at all), the datagram-tag allocation and its reuse for the fragments of one datagram across successive polls, and the RFC 4944 datagram-size rule (the FRAG1 datagram size being 40 octets more than the payload length, fragment offsets multiples of eight except the last) all behave exactly as in the pinned baseline.
rubrics.rationale: These regions border the re-extracted stages and are upstream behavior a careless restructuring can shift; they are the instance-specific residues that a byte-for-byte preservation demand protects even when the suite happens not to assert them.
